content.text: Minette (or Minet) is a traditional 18th-century French card game for two players. It is a point-trick game played with a 32-card Piquet deck, sharing similarities with games like Ã‰cartÃ© and Mariage. It is notable for its 'Exchanges' phase and the focus on capturing specific high-value cards while navigating the constraints of a small deck.
Dates back to at least the early 1700s in France. It was a popular parlor game among the bourgeoisie before being overshadowed by BÃ©zique and Belote.

Two players only. Minette is played exclusively by two players; each is dealt twelve cards and the remaining eight cards form the talon (stock), from which trump is determined. There are no partnerships.
Each player is dealt 12 cards. The remaining 8 cards form a 'Talon' (Stock).

items.text: Standard: Standard two-player Minette with 12 cards each and 8-card talon; trump from talon.
With exchange: Variant allowing players to discard and draw from the talon (exchange phase) before or during play.
No exchange: Play without talon exchange; deal 12 each and play 12 tricks only.
